spans.s:
Udra is the name of an animal occurring only in the list of
sacrificial victims at the Aśvamedha given in the Saṃhitās of
the Yajurveda.^1 According to Mahīdhara^2 it was a crab; but
as the commentary on the Taittirīya Saṃhitā^3 calls it a water-
cat, there can be no doubt that it was an otter.
1) Taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 5, 20, 1;
Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iii. 14, 18; Vāja-
saneyi Saṃhitā, xxiv. 37.
2) On Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, loc. cit.
3) Loc. cit.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 95,
96; Schrader, Prehistoric Antiquities,
247. Udrin occurs in the Baudhāyana
Śrauta Sūtra, ii. 5.
